title: Dehypnotize Yourself from False Beliefs
coreMove: A false belief loses authority when you relax the struggle, expose the old label as a learned suggestion, and rehearse a calmer picture the self-image can accept.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers carrying an old ability label
exampleSpecs.stakes: one visible success can either revise the self-image or be dismissed as luck
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Adler, mathematics, teacher, and classroom problem to show a label breaking

exampleSpecs.stakes: a borrowed norm can make inferiority look objective
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Norton L. Williams, self-realization, individuality, and comparison

exampleSpecs.audience: readers trying to force worry away
exampleSpecs.stakes: willpower can feed the mental loop it is trying to end
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Matthew N. Chappell, worry, willpower, and relaxation

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who treat tension as a willpower failure
exampleSpecs.stakes: muscles need a picture of release, not another order to obey
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use 30 minutes, concrete legs, marionette, and body release

exampleSpecs.audience: readers turning relaxation into another performance
exampleSpecs.stakes: calm becomes unavailable if the practice is judged like a test
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use beach memory, balloons, 30 minutes, and nonresistance

exampleSpecs.audience: high performers who answer inferiority with ranking
exampleSpecs.stakes: winning the comparison can still leave identity dependent on comparison
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: use Norton L. Williams, individuality, self-realization, and comparison
